all.explanation: If true, the server accepts player transfers from other servers via the transfer packet.
If false, players who appear to fly (without elytra/creative) may be kicked by the anti-cheat.
If true, console command output is sent to all online ops.
If true, RCON command output is sent to all online ops.
Custom URL shown in the bug report screen. Empty uses the default Mojang link.
Controls hostile mob damage and hunger drain. hard = mobs deal more damage, hunger can kill.
If true, shows a code-of-conduct popup to players on first join.
Exposes JMX MBeans for monitoring server performance with external tools.
Enables the GameSpy4 query protocol, letting external tools poll server info on query.port.
Enables remote console access (RCON) for sending commands remotely.
If true, the server responds to status pings in the multiplayer server list.
If true, players must have a Mojang-signed key pair. Breaks offline mode if enabled incorrectly.
If true, players removed from whitelist while online are kicked immediately.
Percentage of default entity tracking range. Lower = entities disappear sooner, less bandwidth.
If true, players are forced into the default gamemode every time they (re)join.
Op level required to run commands inside data pack functions (1-4).
Default game mode for new players: survival, creative, adventure, or spectator.
If true, villages, dungeons, temples, etc. generate in new chunks.
JSON object for flat/custom world generation. Only used when level-type is flat or buffet.
If true, players are banned on death and difficulty is locked to hard.
If true, the player list in the server status response is hidden.
Comma-separated list of data packs that are disabled by default on world creation.
Comma-separated list of data packs enabled by default. 'vanilla' is always included.
Name of the world folder on disk.
World generation seed. Empty = random seed chosen at creation.
World type used for generation. minecraft:normal is the standard overworld generator.
If true, player IP addresses are logged when they connect.
Comma-separated allowed origins for the management server HTTP endpoint.
Enables the internal management REST API used by some monitoring tools.
Hostname/IP that the management server binds to.
Port for the management REST API. 0 = auto-assign.
Shared secret for authenticating management server requests.
If true, the management server uses TLS encryption.
Path to the TLS keystore file for the management server.
Password for the management server TLS keystore.
Limits cascading block updates (e.g. redstone chains). Prevents lag from massive chain reactions.
Maximum number of players that can be connected simultaneously.
Milliseconds a single tick can take before the watchdog kills the server. -1 disables the watchdog.
Maximum world border radius in blocks. Limits how far players can travel.
Message of the day displayed in the multiplayer server list.
Packets larger than this (bytes) are compressed. Higher = less CPU, slightly more bandwidth. -1 disables.
If false, the server skips Mojang authentication. Required for offline/cracked clients (EasyAuth handles auth instead).
Default permission level granted to ops (1-4). 4 = full access including /stop.
Seconds after the last player leaves before the server pauses ticking. -1 = never pause.
Minutes of inactivity before a player is kicked. 0 = never kick idle players.
If true, the server blocks connections from known VPN/proxy IPs using the Mojang API.
Port used for the GameSpy4 query protocol (if enable-query is true).
Maximum number of packets a client can send per second. 0 = no limit.
Password required for RCON connections. Empty = RCON disabled even if enable-rcon is true.
Port used for RCON remote console connections.
Compression algorithm for region files. 'deflate' is standard; 'lz4' is faster but uses more disk.
If true, players who decline the server resource pack are disconnected.
URL to a resource pack (.zip) that clients are prompted to download.
UUID identifying the resource pack. Avoids re-downloading if the pack hasn't changed.
Custom message shown when prompting the player to accept the resource pack.
SHA-1 hash of the resource pack file. Used to verify download integrity.
IP address the server binds to. Empty = binds to all available interfaces (0.0.0.0).
The network port the server listens on for player connections.
Chunk radius around each player that is actively ticked (mobs move, crops grow). Lower saves CPU.
Block radius around world spawn where only ops can build/break. 0 disables protection.
Overrides the heartbeat interval for the status endpoint. 0 uses the default.
If true, chunk writes are synchronous (safer but slower). false = async, risks corruption on crash.
Path to a text filtering configuration file for chat message filtering.
Version of the text filtering protocol to use. 0 = default.
If true, uses optimized Linux epoll for networking. Disable if you experience connection issues.
Chunk radius the server sends to each player. Higher = more visible terrain, more bandwidth and memory.
If true, only players listed in whitelist.json can join the server.

all.explanation: Whether in-game time of day advances.
Whether weather patterns change over time.
Whether players can use nether portals to travel between dimensions.
Whether blocks drop items when broken.
Whether some block drops are destroyed by block-caused explosions (TNT).
Whether command blocks show their output in chat.
Whether command blocks can execute commands.
Whether players and mobs take drowning damage.
Whether the server validates elytra flight speed to prevent cheating.
Whether thrown ender pearls disappear when the player dies.
Whether entities (excluding blocks) drop items on death.
Whether players and mobs take fall damage.
Whether players and mobs take fire/lava damage.
Block radius around players within which fire can spread. 0 disables fire spread.
Whether angered neutral mobs stop being angry when the target player dies.
Whether players and mobs take freezing damage from powder snow.
Whether certain sounds (e.g. wither spawning) are heard globally.
Whether players respawn instantly without the death screen.
Whether players keep their inventory and XP on death.
Whether lava can form source blocks (like water does).
Whether players can only craft recipes they have unlocked.
Whether the boss bar / locator bar displays at the top of the screen.
Whether admin commands are logged to the server log.
Maximum number of block changes per tick from commands.
Maximum number of command forks (e.g. /execute) allowed.
Maximum length of a command sequence that can execute in a single tick.
Maximum number of entities that can push into the same block before suffocation damage begins.
Maximum layers of snow that can accumulate from snowfall.
Whether mobs drop loot on death.
Whether some block drops are destroyed by mob-caused explosions (creepers, ghasts).
Whether mobs can modify blocks (creeper explosions, endermen picking up blocks, etc.).
Whether players naturally regenerate health when their hunger bar is full.
Whether the server validates player movement to prevent cheating.
Ticks a creative-mode player must stand in a nether portal before teleporting. 0 = instant.
Ticks a survival/adventure player must stand in a nether portal before teleporting.
Percentage of online players that must sleep to skip the night. 100 = all, 0 = one player suffices.
Whether projectiles (arrows, tridents) can break certain blocks like chorus flowers.
Whether players can deal damage to other players.
Whether raids can spawn when a player with Bad Omen enters a village.
Speed of random block ticks (crop growth, leaf decay, etc.). Default 3, higher = faster.
Whether the debug screen (F3) shows reduced information.
Block radius around the world spawn within which players randomly respawn.
Whether command execution results are shown in chat.
Whether advancement completion messages are broadcast in chat.
Whether death messages are shown in chat.
Whether passive/neutral mobs can spawn naturally.
Whether hostile mobs can spawn naturally.
Whether pillager patrols can spawn.
Whether phantoms can spawn for players who haven't slept.
Whether wandering traders can spawn naturally.
Whether wardens can spawn when triggered by sculk shriekers.
Whether mob spawner blocks can spawn entities.
Whether spectator-mode players cause chunk generation.
Whether vines (and similar blocks) can spread to adjacent surfaces.
Whether TNT blocks explode when ignited.
Whether some block drops are destroyed by TNT explosions.
Whether angered neutral mobs attack all nearby players, not just the one who provoked them.
Whether water can form new source blocks when flowing between two existing sources.
